| [009 - Automated Test Generation Bots](agents/009-automated-test-generation.md)                                                                 | Agent-driven test generation pipeline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [010 - Recipe-Driven Agent Registry](agents/010-recipe-driven-agent-registry.md)                                                                | Goose recipe YAML as the source of truth for agent definitions                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [044 - Code Executor Sandbox Workload and Self-Describing Guest Runtimes](agents/044-code-executor-sandbox.md)                                  | New zero-egress warm-restore `sandbox` fc-invoke workload exposing a `run_python` tool to the Discord concierge and monolith MCP surfaces: the deterministic middle tier between answering from weights and a full goose session. Interpreters follow the trust boundary (baked into the goose guest image, brokered for everything outside a microVM), and every guest image bakes a build-time-generated `/etc/environment.md` so environments are self-describing again post-ADR 040. Accepted |
| [045 - FaaS on the fc-invoke Sandbox Runtime](agents/045-faas-on-fc-invoke-sandbox-runtime.md)                                                  | Register named Python functions and invoke them by URL (`jomcgi.dev/functions/<name>`) on the unchanged zero-egress `sandbox` guest: the framework (registry, routing, request/response marshaling, test-gated ingestion, public/private exposure) lives entirely in the monolith, the guest stays a dumb runtime. Injection not a Postgres import loader (the isolation boundary forbids it); baked-subset deps at v1; workerd/isolates recorded as the future high-density tier. Accepted |
| [046 - MMDS for Dynamic Per-Workload Guest Env](agents/046-mmds-dynamic-workload-env.md)                                                        | Declarative per-workload env in the fc-invoke catalog (Helm values), delivered as boot env plus Firecracker MMDS for the dynamic path: mid-run token/steering updates and per-request data for a persistent process (the semgrep LSP). Host-write-only, no new egress, preserves the zero-egress sandbox. Extends ADR 030. Accepted |

| [012 - Knowledge Gardener Model Pipeline](agents/012-knowledge-gardener-model-pipeline.md)                                                      | Two-tier model pipeline for the knowledge gardener                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [013 - Knowledge Gardener Gemma4-Only](agents/013-knowledge-gardener-gemma4-only.md)                                                            | Single-model pipeline replacement for the gardener                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [014 - AX + Substrate Agent Runtime](agents/014-ax-substrate-agent-runtime.md)                                                                  | Split-roles adoption of google/ax + agent-substrate, retiring orchestrator + cluster_agents                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| [015 - Temporal as Orchestration Substrate](agents/015-temporal-orchestration-substrate.md)                                                     | Adopt Temporal for workflow execution + scheduling; supersedes ADR 014                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| [016 - NATS as Canonical Event Stream](agents/016-nats-canonical-event-stream.md)                                                               | NATS JetStream as the system-wide event bus between independently-owned components                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [017 - Domain Event Schema](agents/017-domain-event-schema.md)                                                                                  | Event envelope schema + tombstone semantics across the system                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [018 - Event-Driven Gardener Triggering](agents/018-event-driven-gardener-trigger.md)                                                           | Monolith pushes gardening sessions via remote-trigger `run` on note edits; drops cron + queue                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| [019 - Substrate Executor + AgentWorkflow over Argo](agents/019-substrate-executor-agentworkflow.md)                                            | Thin Substrate executor interface (agent-sandbox warm pool impl #1) under Argo; revisits 015's warm-pool dismissal for caller-blocked dispatch                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [020 - Deprecate Context Forge](agents/020-deprecate-context-forge-mcp-gateway.md)                                                              | Remove the MCP gateway; serve the monolith's MCP directly (auth stays at the Cloudflare edge). Supersedes 003. Validated plan, deferred execution                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [021 - Discord-Triggered AgentWorkflow with Fast Hosted Model](agents/021-discord-triggered-agentworkflow-fast-model.md)                        | Discord bot (qwen gate) as a new AgentWorkflow consumer riding 019's submit path; fast hosted model (Gemini 3.5 Flash) over an OpenAI-compatible seam; snapshot/resume for smooth many-thread work. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| [022 - Firecracker Snapshot/Restore Controller for AgentWorkflow](agents/022-firecracker-snapshot-restore-controller.md)                        | Build a thin k8s controller (no turnkey OSS exists); FC-direct, porting E2B's architecture; controller owns idle-detect/snapshot/GC/restore-routing/affinity/reconnect, delegates snapshot to Firecracker. Feasibility derisked (28ms restore)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| [023 - Egress Secret Proxy for Agent Sandboxes](agents/023-egress-secret-proxy.md)                                                              | Guest holds only placeholders; real secrets swapped in at the vsock 1025 egress hop (not eBPF: microVM has its own kernel, Go has no OpenSSL). Per-secret allowlist is the exfil control. v1 = TLS-terminating sidecar in the fc-agentd DaemonSet; CRD/operator deferred. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| [024 - Discord Agent, Hosted-Model Tiers, and Isolated Live Artifacts](agents/024-discord-agent-hosted-model-tiers-and-artifacts.md)            | Productive Discord loop on the 022/023 substrate: hosted model via OpenRouter (per-thread knob, key swapped via 023) to beat the 32k Qwen ceiling; two tiers (coding with a gh token vs zero-secret artifact); agent publishes HTML to S3 served in a sandboxed-iframe opaque origin on jomcgi.dev (no subdomain) with ETag hot-reload. Supersedes 021's Argo framing. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [025 - Three-Layer Agent Stack (firecracker-substrate, goosecracker, discord-agent)](agents/025-three-layer-agent-stack-goosecracker.md)        | Name and separate the agent stack into `projects/agents/{firecracker-substrate,goosecracker,discord}`: `firecracker-substrate` (bare microVM primitives, goose-agnostic, opaque `Exec` per 019), `goosecracker` (generic agent manager owning goose recipes + AgentThread snapshot/resume + a generic config surface; depends on the substrate), and `discord` (the Discord agent's workload image/source only). goosecracker stays consumer-agnostic; the Discord agent deploys as a generic goosecracker values config and its runtime glue stays in the monolith bot. Re-bins 022/024 components and re-homes 024 Task 1 tier env into the manager layer; no mechanism change. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [041 - Hot Git Mirror for goosecracker Agent Workspaces](agents/041-hot-git-mirror-agent-workspaces.md)                                         | Hot in-cluster git mirror on node-4 feeding goosecracker agent workspaces: warm base stays repo-agnostic, guests partial-fetch a local always-fresh mirror instead of cold-cloning GitHub on every spin-up; a goosecracker-layer concern per ADR 025, keeping GitHub off the spin-up hot path with no token needed to clone. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [027 - Agent GitHub App Roles: Implementer and Reviewer](agents/027-agent-github-app-roles.md)                                                  | Split the agent's single `gh` identity into two GitHub Apps mapped to roles: a `claude/*`-scoped, no-merge implementer (lower-trust model) and an approve-and-merge reviewer (Opus or better, adversarial spec-vs-impl). Merge gated by a reviewer-controlled `agent-review/gate` status check since App bots cannot be CODEOWNERS; `@jomcgi` stays the human owner. Role token injected per-thread via the 023 egress swap. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [028 - Elastic Agent-MicroVM Capacity and State-Preserving Reclaim](agents/028-elastic-agent-microvm-capacity-and-reclaim.md)                   | Run the disposable agent-microVM tier elastically on a shared node: reaffirm FC-direct (sub-100ms golden-template restore; kata-fc has no CRI snapshot); honest burst via dynamically-sized Guaranteed in-place pod resize + a headroom watermark controller (k8s off the hot path, `Infeasible` resize = spill signal); critical-tenant-safe reclaim via an idle-first victim ladder + graceful drain (checkpoint -> park -> rehydrate) driven by a free-allocatable cushion + node-pinned-Pending watch; and a filesystem-as-durability-contract state model (`/repos` git branches to a state remote, `/data` to S3, rest recomputed) checkpointed as a consistent tuple. Drops per-thread VM snapshots; ballast pods + sharding considered and deferred. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| [030 - fc-invoke, a Single Configurable Surface for Running Workloads in Firecracker](agents/030-fc-invoke-configurable-firecracker-surface.md) | One host daemon that implements ADR 019's stubbed `Substrate.Exec` seam plus the orchestration around it, absorbing `semgrep-scand` and `fc-agentd`'s VM lifecycle. HTTP ingress -> HTTP-over-vsock reverse proxy into a guest; workloads are named Helm-values entries (seven generic knobs: image/resources/concurrency/egress/warmBase/sessioned/requestTimeout); warm-base (platform VM snapshot) and state hydration (guest-side shim capabilities) split on the litmus line; all durable state owned by orchestrators (stateless daemon, 2-way door); a shared bazel-baked guest shim (HTTP server + git/object-store capabilities) keeps the rich guest toolkit out of the thin host contract. Home `projects/firecracker/{substrate,goosecracker,semgrep}`. Supersedes ADR 025 in part. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [031 - Control-Plane / Data-Plane Split for the Agent Substrate (cluster + node)](agents/031-cluster-node-control-data-plane-split.md)          | Split the substrate Go code into a `cluster/` control plane (ingress, catalog, future placement + fleet/in-place-resize) and a `node/` data plane (invoker, fcvm driver, vsockhttp, egress), bracketed by a neutral `substrate.NodeExecutor` seam so neither plane imports the other. One binary/Deployment now (in-process local executor); the physical split to a central agent plus per-node DaemonSet later is a wiring change behind the seam, not a rewrite. Accepted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [032 - Warm-Snapshot Bazel Worker as an MCP Tool Surface](agents/032-warm-bazel-worker-mcp.md)                                                  | A `bazel` fc-invoke workload whose warm base holds a live Bazel server with the `//...` analysis graph resident (the in-memory Skyframe state no runner can otherwise persist), exposed to any OAuth'd Claude session as monolith MCP tools (`bazel-query`/`bazel-test`/`bazel-status`). Analysis local against the hot graph, execution/caching remote on BuildBuddy RBE; sessioned clones live between calls for a sub-second loop; dirty trees travel as `refs/agents/**` scratch refs on the hot mirror; base rebuilds are chained and triggered by measured analysis-phase time, never saved back from serving clones. Requires devmapper CoW rootfs, a post-restore clock step, and the API key via the egress proxy. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [033 - Golden-Template Distribution via Daemon-Pulled OCI Artifacts](agents/033-golden-template-distribution-daemon-pulled-oci.md)              | Node daemons pull golden templates as content-addressed OCI artifacts and reconcile them into local devpool against a per-CPU-pool desired set published by the control plane. Decouples template lifecycle from node/pod lifecycle: publishing or swapping a template is a desired-set change, not a node roll or pod restart. OCI image-volume mount rejected (immutable per pod); raw S3 rejected for templates (no native content-addressing). Compatibility key is (CPU-template baseline, FC snapshot version); the desired-set write path is the real trust root. Accepted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [034 - Per-Tier MCP Tool ACLs for Goosecracker Guests](agents/034-per-tier-guest-mcp-acl.md)                                                    | Guest-facing MCP moves to monolith-owned per-tier endpoints (/private/mcp/{tier}/) authenticated by per-tier bearer tokens carried via the ADR 023 placeholder swap; one K8s Secret is the rotatable source of truth for both the monolith validator and the substrate swap catalog. Closes the unauthenticated monolith:8000 /mcp bypass by moving the progress/artifact sink to the guest-facing service and removing the blanket allowlist entry. Context Forge virtual servers rejected (paths are not boundaries, third-party token-scoping trust); network-only isolation rejected (needs per-connection tier attribution); workload-per-tier kept as the credential-free escape hatch. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [035 - Discord Multiplayer Agent UX (Ambient Classifier, Thread Sessions, Live Task Checklist)](agents/035-discord-multiplayer-agent-ux.md)     | Make the Discord agent surface thread-native, legible, and steerable, closing the three interaction gaps a Claude Tag evaluation surfaced: a two-stage classifier (mention-guaranteed attention plus per-channel ambient standing instructions stored as ADR 029 grants; depth routed by the first conversational turn via the sub-recipe router's new "just chat" branch), a conversational ack (concierge reply) followed by a live task checklist edited in place at stage boundaries by the progress reconciler, and thread-scoped shared sessions that accept in-order steering messages from anyone in the thread (per-author tier checks apply). Channel behaviour is a living directive: git seeds the initial prompt, the operative per-channel directive (plus per-user style preferences) evolves in Postgres from attributed interaction feedback with provenance, resettable to the git seed; directives shape style only and can never touch tools, ACLs, or ambient enablement. Per-message ML relevance classifier, one-message-per-stage progress, token streaming, combined ack+checklist message, and git-tracked directives rejected. Channel-data tools deferred to a later ADR. Accepted    |
| [036 - Orchestrator Brief-Compiler Tier via OpenRouter](agents/036-orchestrator-brief-compiler-tier.md)                                         | Add a host-side orchestrator to the monolith chat harness that runs only on escalations: it routes chat vs goose before any microVM boots (ADR 035 Phase 4 chat branch is built behind this seam, not in agent.yaml) and compiles a grounded task brief (recipe route, repo paths, structure hints, done criteria, initial stage plan) for the local Qwen executor. Orchestrator model accessed via OpenRouter (1Password-managed key, model = values config, default DeepSeek-flash class); prompt assembled deterministically with a build-time-baked stable prefix (base prompt + recipe catalog + repo structure digest) first and volatile context last, to maximise provider cache hits; grounding from the recipe catalog, repo docs manifest, and KG; no tools, retrieval-in text-out; briefs are advisory (recipes/ACLs still constrain execution) and logged for brief-vs-execution attribution. Fail-open to direct submit when down or ungranted; per-server/channel consent grant gates external-API use; attention classification and all chat replies stay local-Qwen-only for cost. Bigger local orchestrator, Claude CLI hot path, direct DeepSeek API, and frontier executor rejected. Accepted |
| [037 - Label-Driven Firecracker Node Enrollment](agents/037-label-driven-firecracker-node-enrollment.md)                                        | Enroll FC-capable nodes by label (`homelab.io/firecracker=true`) instead of the node-4-specific kata-fc ritual: the fc-invoke daemon self-identifies its node via the downward API (`spec.nodeName`) and derives arch from `runtime.GOARCH`, so relabeling a node needs no chart edit. Retires the five `sudo bash` setup scripts and the `kata-fc` RuntimeClass. Accepted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| [038 - Autonomous Work Queue with Capability-Tier Routing and Reviewer-Verdict Feedback](agents/038-autonomous-work-queue-tiered-gating.md)     | A Postgres work queue drained by a scheduler job into goosecracker dispatch keeps 2-3 local-Qwen agent slots saturated with feeder-produced work (loom code-health register diffs, CI red-run diagnosis, Renovate triage, STPA staleness, plans triage). Every task class carries a verification mode and a minimum implementer tier: machine-verified work runs on Qwen, advisory output skips PRs entirely, judgment work (STPA authorship) floors at Opus. All merges flow through the ADR 027 implementer/reviewer gate with forced review semantics (APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES, `agent:rejected` / `agent:requeue` labels), and a verdict ledger feeds /improve-recipes and auto-demotes task classes whose merge rate falls. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| [039 - WhatsApp Channel Gateway (whatsmeow) for the Household Agent](agents/039-whatsapp-channel-gateway.md)                                    | Add WhatsApp as a second channel onto the goosecracker agent stack: a dedicated throwaway number joins a three-participant group (Joe, partner, bot), served by a transport-only Go gateway under `projects/monolith/whatsapp/` embedding whatsmeow (session in a dedicated Postgres schema). Inbound goes to the monolith chat pipeline (ADR 035 attention/depth reused); outbound drains a `chat.whatsapp_outbox` mirroring the Discord outbox; sessions are group-keyed (no threads: one active session per group, reply steering). A new `household` trust tier grants explicit-confirmed knowledge capture, calendar, Q&A, and digests, but no repo/cluster/artifact tools. Official Business API, linking Joe's own number, Baileys gateways, Python wrappers, Matrix bridging, and a channel-abstraction-first refactor all rejected. Accepted                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| [040 - Caller-Provided Context Injection for Agent Guests (`/injected-context/`)](agents/040-caller-provided-context-injection.md)              | Give agent guests a third opaque hydration input alongside `task` and `sessionDb`: an `injectedContext` file bundle the guest unpacks to `/injected-context/`, so an agent can grep caller-side context (e.g. a prior Discord conversation) that is neither in the repo nor in its own session. The substrate, fc-invoke daemon, and guest handler stay context-agnostic (pure transport, opaque bundle); only a `chat.api.build_injected_context(session, tier)` provider knows the source, tier-filters the messages, and writes a self-describing `README.md`. The bundle is rebuilt inside the per-turn `run_and_deliver` loop so it persists and accumulates across turns on ephemeral tmpfs. Prompt-stuffing (token-bound), git-mirror carriage (transcripts in permanent history), a chat-specific payload field (couples the substrate), prompt-carried provenance (silent invisible files), and live-mutating a warm guest (guests are ephemeral) all rejected. Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |

## Chat

| ADR                                                                            | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |

| [001 - Ambient Feedback Loop and Directive Autopilot](chat/001-improve-ambient-loop.md) | Score ambient Discord activations from attention decisions, reactions, and follow-up. Code levers (prompt, gate, reply voice) change only through a human-reviewed evidence-backed skill; reversible directive levers (channel directives, per-user style prefs) go autonomous via a silent self-validating autopilot. Three-level routing (global / channel / personal), source precedence (manual wins), guard() constraint. Accepted |

## Docs

| ADR                                                                                                               | Decision                                                                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [001 - Static Docs Site](docs/001-static-docs-site.md)                                                            | VitePress for architecture documentation (superseded by 002)                                                   |
| [002 - Retire Standalone Web Frontends, Docs into Monolith](docs/002-websites-decommission-docs-into-monolith.md) | Delete `projects/websites/` + trips/hikes Pages frontends; serve docs from the monolith at `jomcgi.dev/docs/*` |

## EmberVM

| ADR                                                                                                     | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [001 - EmberVM, a BEAM Orchestrator for Firecracker Workloads](embervm/001-embervm-beam-firecracker-workload-orchestrator.md) | Generalize the fc-invoke/FaaS line into EmberVM: a standalone, open-sourceable Elixir control plane over the Firecracker fleet with a Go node daemon. Hit/miss invariant (control plane on the invocation path only for lifecycle actions); ETS hot set + pluggable durable op-log (SQLite default / ra HA); Workload CRD for definitions, op-log for executions; uniform HTTP wire contract; no-cross-principal isolation rule; level-triggered capacity contract; roadmap of workload classes (tasks, zip, sessions, serving, stateful, composite), no rung shipping without a first consumer. Accepted; R0 shipped 2026-07-14 |
| [002 - Op-Log Retention and Compaction Policy](embervm/002-op-log-retention-and-compaction.md) | Bound the op-log SQLite database: result TTLs enforced at read and dedupe time (never served stale), projections swept hourly (expired results, terminal tasks past 7-day retention), and the append-only ops journal prefix-compacted past a 30-day horizon behind a durable `compacted_through_seq` marker so the ra tier and R6 facade can still trust replay semantics. Long-horizon audit delegates to SigNoz; a PVC watermark alert replaces discovery-by-outage. Accepted |
| [003 - Control-Plane-Managed Snapshot Distribution and Eviction](embervm/003-control-plane-managed-snapshot-distribution.md) | Base snapshots become content-addressed portable artifacts (enabled by R1 vsock hydration) that the control plane places for utilization, extending its existing placement authority. The node exposes verbs, never decisions: `RestoreBase` (warm-pull from a SeaweedFS object store), `ExportBase` (persist off-node), `EvictBase` (drain-guarded removal for stale/redistributed/superseded bases). `BuildBase` stays the build-if-not-in-store fallback. Control loop: demand + capacity -> desired placement -> build/pull/evict -> dispatch to the best-placed warm node. `EvictBase` also fixes the today gap where re-registration orphans old base bundles. Accepted |
| [004 - Back the Kubernetes agent-sandbox Interface with the EmberVM Substrate](embervm/004-agent-sandbox-interface-compatibility.md) | Treat kubernetes-sigs/agent-sandbox as the intended external interface for EmberVM's R2 session/sandbox class rather than building a competing native API. Do not implement its CRDs in ember's core; a deferred, gated adapter (a thin K8s controller) owns the per-instance Sandbox/SandboxClaim objects at the edge and translates to ember session lifecycle, keeping ember's core on low-churn definitions plus the node contract. Only obligation on R2 now: shape the session seam so the adapter is a translation layer, not a redesign. Accepted |
| [005 - EmberVM Scale-Out on EKS (metal pool, bricks, EmberPool CRD)](embervm/005-embervm-eks-scale-out-metal-pool-bricks.md) | Scale EmberVM to a max-utilization EKS deployment. Firecracker forces a metal-only, untainted, mixed-family NodePool; capacity is a portfolio of T-shirt-sized daemon "bricks" the kube-scheduler bin-packs (a Pending brick is the only Karpenter scale-up signal), chosen over autoscaler-invisible in-place resize. An EmberPool CRD (Ember controller = single writer of replicas) reconciles a per-(arch, size-class) count vector from known-load (exact offline bin-pack) + forecast residual (TimesFM) + reactive buffer. Guest base as a digest-pinned OCI image (Pattern A), primed snapshots keyed by (arch, CPU, kernel, base-digest); default-priority, de-privileged bricks. Accepted |
| [006 - TLA+ Formal Specification Pilot for Concurrency-Critical Protocols](embervm/006-tla-formal-specification-pilot.md) | Pilot small per-protocol TLA+/PlusCal specs for EmberVM's highest-risk protocols, deferred until the remaining feature rungs are live: VM lifecycle + adoption first (the dispatch-restart-wedge lineage), session bank/relight and the quota gate contingent on the pilot earning its keep. Model honesty is the core of the decision: three conformance layers (CI vocabulary sync tests against proto/FSM/op-log surfaces, op-log trace validation via TLC trace checking, and a scheduled stpa-style review skill) keep the specs demonstrably in sync, with an explicit exit judgment if they don't pay. Whole-system specs rejected; StreamData property testing kept as the complement for Elixir-local logic. Accepted |
| [007 - Sharded Control Plane, Batched Postgres Op-Log Tier and Cell Architecture](embervm/007-sharded-control-plane-pg-oplog-cells.md) | Retire the control plane's scale ceilings found reviewing EmberVM against Modal/Fly.io/fleet-scale-K8s: the durable tier becomes batched (group-commit) Postgres through the existing op-log seam (CNPG homelab, managed Pg on EKS; SQLite stays the zero-dep single-node default; `ra` parked for R6), making control-plane pods stateless. Horizontal scaling is cells (bounded, single-writer control planes owning their bricks and workloads; one op-log appender per cell solves multi-writer seq ordering) under a thin stateless fleet layer deferred until >1 cell. Build-now seams: `cell_id` in schema and registry keying, workload-to-cell assignment as data, per-cell dial-home address. Plus decided fixes for the review's hot-loop findings: dispatcher O(V^2) adopt sweep, full-state heartbeat fan-in, timer-driven full-table reconciles, global prime/bank caps, first-fit task placement, serial xDS PUTs, per-VM nftables full-table regen. Accepted |
| [008 - Interruptible Bank for Scale-to-Zero Stateful Datastores](embervm/008-interruptible-bank-stateful-datastores.md) | A per-workload, opt-in interruptible bank mode (default off, atomic bank unchanged) so a latency-sensitive datastore never cold-boots in steady state. The bank becomes two-phase and abortable: a connection arriving during the snapshot resumes the paused VM (hot, same generation, no churn) and discards the temp snapshot, while a clean bank commits and the next wake warm-restores. Driver primitives (Pause/Resume/CreateSnapshot/LoadSnapshot) already exist; correctness rests on keeping only a snapshot taken immediately before teardown and discarding any whose VM resumed, which the generation-pairing invariant already enforces; decision-7 keeps in-flight queries unfrozen and racing connections parked, not rejected. Opt-in contains the TLA+ bank-relight invariant delta to the workloads that ask for it. Draft |
| [009 - Roadmap Extension, Continuity Before Tenancy](embervm/009-roadmap-extension-continuity-before-tenancy.md) | Defer the R6 Facade (etcd shim, virtual control planes, hard multi-tenancy) from Future ADR to Recorded, revived only on real demand for virtual control planes or external tenants, and extend ADR 001's ladder with four rungs (amended same day): R6 Continuity (a routine noded or control-plane roll never loses committed data and never cold-boots a stateful workload; state portable and durable within ISA/CPU and volume-anchoring bounds), R7 Distribution (redistribute and pre-warm workloads across many nodes; placement is a copy, never a rebuild; needs a second Firecracker-capable node), R8 Consumers (agent-thread tier on EmberVM sessions, retiring fc-agentd), R9 Packaging (standalone open-sourceable artifact). The v1 availability contract is spot-instance semantics with a two-minute preemption bound, softening R4's never-severed invariant to never-severed-except-by-bounded-preemption; state durability stays the hard guarantee behind a configurable S3-API object store (SeaweedFS first backend), which is also ADR 003's first honest consumer of its export/restore verbs. Accepted |
| [010 - Bazel Skyframe Snapshot as a Stateless Query Demo](embervm/010-bazel-skyframe-snapshot-query-demo.md) | A public `/ember` demo proving Skyframe efficiency: Bazel's loading+analysis graph lives in a local, single-server JVM heap that RBE cannot cache (RBE caches execution only), so a cold server re-pays full analysis (Abseil 13.8s, a monorepo minutes) before RBE is ever consulted; Skycache is Blaze-internal with no OSS backend. Snapshot the warm server as a base and serve each request from a disposable copy-on-write clone that runs one read-only `bazel cquery` then reaps, so the lifecycle is request-response-reap with zero persisted state and RBE kept as-is (recorded) for execution. Interactive tier Abseil (~0.6GB base, ~200MB heap, zero-egress, expression-only input), headline/scale tier Envoy (multi-GB heap) measured on Linux. Reuses ADR 003/009 snapshot artifacts and R7 copy-not-rebuild relight; no new node verbs. Silent-failure guards: snapshot after the warming client exits, serving flags must equal warming flags or the analysis cache is discarded. Draft |
| [011 - Distribution via Longhorn Volumes, Single-Writer Fencing, and CP-Sequenced Rollouts](embervm/011-distribution-longhorn-fencing-cp-rollouts.md) | Shape R7 Distribution (decided in ADR 009) around three findings: the fleet constraint is Firecracker snapshot portability, not KVM, so noded runs on all 4 nodes with vendor-keyed warmth (AMD node-4 warm tier, Intel nodes cold/failover; volumes portable, sessions vendor-pinned), dissolving the second-FC-node hardware prerequisite. Stateful volumes move to Longhorn RWO node-attach (block device to Firecracker; StorageClass durability tiers; bank commits become Longhorn snapshots with incremental S3 backup), retiring the custom vol.img export and rejecting dm-thin/manifest/RWX alternatives. Single-writer HA: the CP arbitrates placement (election free via single-flight) while Longhorn attach exclusivity is the physical fence and generation blessing (CP the sole issuer; unblessed artifacts quarantined) fences the warmth plane before a second warm node exists. noded rolls become CP-sequenced OnDelete (interlocks, drain, delete, verify; staleness bound and CP-down fallback mandatory). Resolves ADR 003's open placement-policy question vendor-aware; CP owns WHEN, k8s/Longhorn/S3 own HOW. Accepted |
| [012 - Fleet Co-Location on the etcd Masters and CP-Managed Dynamic Sizing](embervm/012-fleet-colocation-cp-dynamic-sizing.md) | The fleet is the four existing nodes: Firecracker guests co-locate on the three Intel etcd masters alongside node-4, with the etcd blast radius explicitly accepted (GitOps-reconstructible cluster, durable state in S3). Guest capacity becomes scheduler-visible via a CP-owned in-place resize loop (grow-eager / shrink-lazy, resize-not-satisfiable = placement refusal), replacing static maxLiveVMs sizing; no hard FC taint. Two permanent vendor snapshot pools (Intel masters, AMD node-4) with a grandfather rule keeping unstamped legacy artifacts restorable on their home node. Reconstructible cache stays node-local hostPath; Longhorn only for live pg volumes. Target is CP-authored per-node noded Deployments with a DaemonSet bridge until then; registry persists to NVMe so a warm node never goes dead on a brief CP outage. Accepted |
| [013 - Substrate Lanes, Brick Sizing, and the Capacity Tier Ladder](embervm/013-substrate-lanes-brick-sizing-capacity-tiers.md) | Landscape response: classes are reuse semantics, substrates are lanes under them. urunc rejected (CRI pod-per-invocation is the path ADR 001 bypasses); wasm is a demand-gated source lane run inside the FC guest, never in-process on the host; Hyperlight recorded as a task-class substrate option (Rust brick daemon, no warmth machinery) plus a possible future per-request-isolated serving class. Brick sizing rule refining 005: a brick is 4-8x the largest VM of its class, a handful per node, two classes to start; per-brick contiguous headroom is a first-class ledger dimension (aggregates lie for refill). Capacity tier ladder reconciling 005 with 012: resize tier on fixed fleets, brick tier on autoscaled pools, one budget-agnostic binary, tier chosen by deployment. Accepted |
| [014 - Worker-Authoritative State and a Hot-Path Consistency Model](embervm/014-worker-authoritative-state-hot-path-consistency.md) | Adopt the Modal-style consistency split for the CP: node-agent dial-home reports become the source of truth for instance runtime state (CP tables a reconciled cache, removing the drift bug class behind the alias-misroute and adoption-wedge incidents), durable writes come off the boot/wake hot paths (metering stays synchronous fail-closed), placement becomes advisory reject/retry across bricks, and tap/netlink plumbing is pre-provisioned at brick boot. Two consistency carve-outs: the destroyed transition is node-confirmed only with fail-closed reconciliation toward destruction, and a new `isolated_execution: true` workload flag makes single-use a platform-enforced contract (no pool return, relight, or snapshot capture) for security-scanning and multi-tenant workloads. Draft |
| [015 - Isolated High-Throughput Lane with Data-Plane Placement](embervm/015-isolated-high-throughput-lane-data-plane-placement.md) | A third lane combining the serving lane's transport with the task lane's semantics for high-throughput totally-isolated requests: Envoy routes straight to per-brick listeners (no control-plane hop per request), the node agent pops a fresh primed microVM per request, runs it, and destroys it node-confirmed, re-priming in the background, so single-use isolation is structural to the lane rather than the cross-lane `isolated_execution` flag ADR 014 decision 6 proposed (this ADR replaces that mechanism). Balancing is data-plane: LEAST_REQUEST across bricks, instant 503 on an empty pool, Envoy bounded retry and outlier ejection, replacing today's weightless ROUND_ROBIN. Metering stays fail-closed via per-brick quota leases renewed on the dial-home cadence. The CP becomes a pure control loop: pool sizing, lease grants, xDS publication, reconcile from reports. Draft |
| [016 - Kubernetes Scheduling Integration Contract: Drive the Autoscaler, Own VM Placement](embervm/016-kubernetes-scheduling-integration-contract.md) | Answers import-vs-rebuild for the kube-scheduler/Karpenter overlap: neither; integrate through the pod ABI with three layers, three owners (CP owns VM-to-brick via filter/score/bind over the per-brick ledger; kube-scheduler owns brick-to-node shaped only by pod spec; Karpenter/NAP own nodes driven by Pending bricks). Encodes per-environment behavioral contracts (EKS spreads at placement so consolidation is the real bin-packer; GKE optimize-utilization packs; homelab pages) and makes consolidation compatibility a lane admission requirement (drain on SIGTERM, do-not-disrupt only while occupied, disruption budgets). Priority projection: PriorityClass ranks brick pools per lane (below-default only for lanes with proven drain), Guaranteed QoS protects running bricks, workload priority lives in CP dispatch; balloon bricks are the only sacrificial pods; the lane-to-PriorityClass ladder is a CP-owned table (workload registration is headed Helm-or-API with durable CP-datastore definitions) while the PriorityClass rungs themselves stay chart-managed. Packing policy: class-exact placement, score bin-packs toward empty bricks so reclaim cascades (empty brick, shrink count, node consolidation); isolated lane spreads by design in the data plane. Node lifecycle is a placement input: two disruption postures (preemptible vs durable with an 8h per-session continuity guarantee delivered by HA banked state, not node pinning), remaining node lifetime as a ledger fact, terminating nodes kept utilized by fit-checked durable or preferential preemptible placement, schedule-gated per-lane budgets with grace periods derived from measured bank time; users express posture only (preemptible/durable + lane + duration under the 8h ceiling, sized for long coding sessions), all raw scheduling mechanics platform-derived and non-escalatable; session contract is three-tier (8h live ceiling bounded by placement; 7-day S3 memory-snapshot resume window, unexpired banks are GC roots; 30-day durable workspace of zstd content-addressed files captured eagerly at every bank, resumed via base + hydration, vendor/generation-unpinned) behind one four-verb resume interface (cold, base restore, warm relight, base + workspace hydration) where the CP picks the cheapest unexpired artifact. EKS/Karpenter proven first (metal today; EC2 nested-virt on 7i/8i is a watched cost lever gated on the provisioning paths exposing the CPU option; GKE Standard nested-virt demand-gated, Autopilot excluded); contracts drilled via Karpenter's kwok provider, path-scoped in CI to the Karpenter-facing modules only, with the drain/migration protocol a TLA+ pilot candidate. Secondary scheduler and predictive simulators recorded as reserved options. Draft |

# ADR 001: Reduce Cloudflare Operator Scope via Envoy Gateway

**Author:** Joe McGinley
**Status:** Implemented
**Created:** 2026-02-28
**Relates to:** [K8s API Tunnel RFC](../../../docs/plans/2026-02-26-k8s-api-tunnel.md)

---

## Problem

The Cloudflare operator (`operators/cloudflare/`) has grown to 6 controllers and 2 CRDs:

| Controller               | Responsibility                                                                            |
| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GatewayClass`           | Validates credentials, sets Accepted condition                                            |
| `Gateway`                | Creates `CloudflareTunnel` CRD, deploys `cloudflared` Deployment + HPA + PDB              |
| `CloudflareTunnel`       | Full state machine for Cloudflare tunnel API lifecycle (create/delete/credentials)        |
| `HTTPRoute`              | Resolves backends, creates Cloudflare published routes + DNS CNAME records                |
| `CloudflareAccessPolicy` | Manages Cloudflare Zero Trust access applications (GEP-713 policy attachment)             |
| `Service`                | Convenience layer — annotation-driven auto-creation of Gateway + HTTPRoute + AccessPolicy |

This reimplements routing primitives (listener config, backend resolution, route matching) that Envoy Gateway handles natively. Meanwhile, production traffic still runs through the static `cloudflare-tunnel` Helm chart (`overlays/prod/cloudflare-tunnel/values.yaml`) with 12 hardcoded routes — the operator isn't serving production yet.

The operator's Gateway API implementation is also incomplete: it uses a custom `cloudflare` GatewayClass rather than conforming to a real data-plane implementation, so HTTPRoutes don't get actual in-cluster load balancing — `cloudflared` proxies directly to backend Services.

---

## Decision

Replace the operator's in-cluster routing with Envoy Gateway and reduce the operator to Cloudflare-side lifecycle only.

### Layer 1 — Envoy Gateway (upstream, not owned)

Envoy Gateway provides a conformant Gateway API implementation:

- `Gateway` resources per trust boundary (public, private)
- `HTTPRoute` resources for per-app routing with real in-cluster load balancing
- TLS termination, header/path matching, traffic splitting — all upstream

This replaces the operator's `GatewayClass`, `Gateway`, `HTTPRoute`, and `Service` controllers entirely.

### Layer 2 — Cloudflare Operator (reduced scope)

Three CRDs remain:

| CRD                      | Responsibility                                                                                    |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `CloudflareTunnel`       | Manages tunnel API lifecycle, deploys `cloudflared` pointing at an Envoy Gateway Service endpoint |
| `CloudflareDNSRecord`    | Manages Cloudflare DNS CNAME records (currently embedded in HTTPRoute controller)                 |
| `CloudflareAccessPolicy` | Manages Cloudflare Zero Trust access applications (unchanged)                                     |

The tunnel-to-gateway mapping is one tunnel per Gateway — `cloudflared` points at the Envoy Gateway Service instead of resolving backends directly.

### What Gets Deleted

| Current                                                  | Replacement                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GatewayClass` controller                                | Envoy Gateway's GatewayClass                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `Gateway` controller (tunnel + deployment orchestration) | `CloudflareTunnel` CRD refs an Envoy Gateway; deployment orchestration (`ensureCloudflaredDeployment`, HPA, PDB, `DefaultCloudflaredReplicas`) migrates from `gateway_controller.go` into `CloudflareTunnel` controller |
| `HTTPRoute` controller (DNS + published routes)          | Envoy Gateway handles routing; `CloudflareDNSRecord` CRD handles DNS                                                                                                                                                    |
| `Service` controller (annotation convenience)            | Removed — teams create HTTPRoute + CloudflareDNSRecord directly                                                                                                                                                         |
| Published routes API calls                               | Removed — `cloudflared` uses `--url` pointing at gateway, no per-route config                                                                                                                                           |

### What Changes in `CloudflareTunnel`

```diff
 CloudflareTunnelSpec:
   name:         string
   accountId:    string
-  configSource: string        # removed — no more Cloudflare-side route config
-  ingress:      []TunnelIngress  # removed — Envoy Gateway handles routing
+  gatewayRef:                 # ref to the Envoy Gateway resource
+    name:       string
+    namespace:  string
+  replicas:     int           # cloudflared deployment sizing (currently hardcoded at 2)
```

### New CRD: `CloudflareDNSRecord`

```yaml
CloudflareDNSRecord:
  spec:
    tunnelRef:
      name: string # ref to CloudflareTunnel
    hostname: string # e.g. app.jomcgi.dev
    proxied: bool # Cloudflare proxy enabled
```

Replaces the DNS record management currently embedded in the HTTPRoute controller (lines that call `CreateTunnelDNSRecord` and store record IDs in annotations).

---

## Migration Path

### Phase 1 — Validate with Static Config

No operator changes. Deploy Envoy Gateway alongside the existing `cloudflare-tunnel` chart:

1. Install Envoy Gateway, create a `Gateway` resource with HTTPS listener
2. Create `HTTPRoute` resources for 2-3 services (e.g. `argocd.jomcgi.dev`, `signoz.jomcgi.dev`)
3. Point the existing `cloudflared` at the Envoy Gateway Service instead of direct backends
4. Remove the migrated routes from `overlays/prod/cloudflare-tunnel/values.yaml`
5. Verify: traffic still flows, latency is acceptable, Linkerd mesh compatibility works

**Success criteria:** routing changes require only `HTTPRoute` edits, no tunnel config changes.

### Phase 2 — Build Reduced-Scope CRDs

Modify existing `CloudflareTunnel` CRD to add `gatewayRef`, remove `ingress`. Build `CloudflareDNSRecord` CRD. Delete the `GatewayClass`, `Gateway`, `HTTPRoute`, and `Service` controllers.

### Phase 3 — Full Migration

Migrate all 12 static routes from the `cloudflare-tunnel` chart to `HTTPRoute` + `CloudflareDNSRecord` resources. Deprecate the static chart.

---

## Consequences

- **Short-term:** Envoy Gateway adds a new cluster dependency (~2 pods). Existing static tunnel chart continues working during migration.
- **Medium-term:** Operator codebase shrinks from 6 controllers to 3. Routing becomes portable Gateway API resources.
- **Long-term:** In-cluster routing is upstream-maintained. Operator owns only Cloudflare API integration.

### Open Questions

1. **Envoy Gateway + Linkerd** — the cluster runs Linkerd service mesh. Need to verify Envoy Gateway pods get meshed correctly and don't conflict with Linkerd's proxy injection.
2. **Resource overhead** — Envoy Gateway runs its own Envoy fleet. On a 5-node homelab cluster, need to size this appropriately (single replica with HPA may be sufficient).
3. **Public/private split** — the ADR assumes two Gateways for trust boundaries. Current setup is single tunnel for everything. Evaluate whether the split is worth the complexity for a homelab.
title: ADR 001: Reduce Cloudflare Operator Scope via Envoy Gateway
